summary: Join our training course on satellite imagery and learn to monitor climate change effectively. Equip yourself with essential skills for a sustainable future!
lede: Satellite imagery supports climate change monitoring by helping teams track environmental change and build climate indicators. Designed for GIS specialists, remote-sensing analysts, climate-risk officers, and environmental consultants, this training develops practical workflows for assessing hazards and communicating evidence. Learners prepare imagery, calculate vegetation and burn indicators, interpret time series and change detection, and document uncertainty through validation records and maps.
audienceIntro: Satellite imagery and climate change monitoring training suits professionals who work with environmental evidence, spatial data, climate risk, or land and ecosystem decisions. It supports foundation-to-intermediate development for people who need practical analysis without becoming specialist remote-sensing programmers.
prerequisites: This course suits foundation-to-intermediate learners with basic computer literacy and an interest in GIS, environmental monitoring, climate risk, or remote sensing. Prior exposure to maps, spreadsheets, or environmental datasets helps but is not required. No programming experience is required for completion. Google Earth Engine scripting appears through prepared templates and guided demonstrations, while QGIS exercises focus on operational application rather than technical engineering. A laptop with QGIS installed is recommended; browser access supports Google Earth Engine and NASA Worldview activities.
